cards.text: Alright, friend, grab an apron and pull up a stool. Jesus leaves where He's been and goes to the region of Tyre. He goes into a house, and He doesn't want anyone to know He's there.

cards.question: Jesus slips into a house in the region of Tyre and manages to keep His visit a secret.

cards.text: Friend, I sat in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS and nobody came looking. Jesus walks into ONE house, and soon a mom whose little daughter has an unclean spirit hears He's there.

cards.question: A mom whose little daughter has an unclean spirit hears Jesus is in the region of Tyre. What does she do when she gets to Him?

answers.text: She sends word to His disciples

cards.text: So who is this mom? Mark tells us she's a Greek woman of Syrophoenician origin.

cards.question: The Syrophoenician woman ___ asking Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter.

cards.text: Then Jesus answers her with a picture from the dinner table. “First let the children have their fill,” He said. “For it is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs.”
Now watch this mom, friend. She doesn't walk away. Her answer starts with “Yes, Lord,” and she's not done.

cards.question: The Syrophoenician woman answers Jesus' picture of the children's bread. What does she point out?

answers.text: Even the dogs under the table eat the crumbs
The children are already full of bread
The dogs can wait until the next meal

cards.text: Friend, my best comebacks show up three days LATE. Hers shows up right on time, and Jesus tells her, “Because of this answer, you may go.”

cards.question: Jesus tells the Syrophoenician woman, “Because of this answer, you may go.” What else does He tell her?

answers.text: The demon has left your daughter
Bring your daughter here to Me
Your daughter will be well in three days

cards.question: When the Syrophoenician woman gets home, she finds her child lying on the bed and the demon gone.

cards.text: Then Jesus leaves the region of Tyre and goes through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, into the region of the Decapolis. Friend, I need a NAP just reading that route.
There's a crowd around Jesus, and some people bring Him a man who is deaf and hardly able to speak. And they don't just ask. They beg.

cards.question: People bring Jesus a man who is deaf and hardly able to speak. What do they beg Jesus to do?

answers.text: Pray for him at the synagogue

cards.question: Jesus heals the deaf man right there in the middle of the crowd.

cards.text: So Jesus takes the man aside privately, away from the crowd. And then He gets hands-on.

cards.question: Jesus has taken the deaf man aside, away from the crowd. Which two places does Jesus touch?

cards.text: Fingers in the man's ears, then Jesus spits and touches his tongue. Then He looks up to heaven and sighs deeply.

cards.question: Jesus says one word to the deaf man: “Ephphatha!” It means “Be ___!”
After Jesus says “Ephphatha!” the man's hearing and speech come back slowly over the next few days.

cards.text: IMMEDIATELY his ears are opened, his tongue is released, and he's speaking plainly. No warm-up, friend, and I can't even say good morning to my oven without clearing my throat twice.
Then Jesus orders them not to tell anyone. Not a word.

cards.question: Jesus orders the people not to tell anyone about the deaf man's healing. What happens?

answers.text: The more He orders them the more they tell it
They keep it to themselves for a while
They tell only their own families

cards.text: Friend, telling people NOT to share news is the fastest way to get it into every group chat in town. And the people are utterly astonished.

cards.question: The astonished people say, “He has done all things well!” They say He makes even the deaf ___ and the mute ___.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards indicates whether the woman asks repeatedly, stops asking, or fears asking; the preceding story card only gives her origin. The baker can only guess the unseen word "kept," rather than reason out its meaning from the setup.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
